The cubic is real and failable -- the down block is a 3x3x4 tensor, so Y_d(h) is linear in h and det Y_d(h) is a genuine non-degenerate cubic form on the P^3 -- but the COUNTING kills the route: one polynomial equation cuts exactly one dimension, so {det Y_d = 0} is a cubic SURFACE (dim 3 -> 2), not points; its singular locus is empty (no nontrivial grad = 0; 5/5 random samples smooth, plus the classical genericity fact), so 'h is a singular point' selects nothing; and the rank<=1 locus has codimension 4 inside dimension 3, empty by count. B1160's recipe does not transfer because there THREE LINEAR anomaly conditions did four dimensions of work first and the cubic only cut a LINE to points.
kill_form: dimension-count (one cubic cuts one of three dimensions; the missing ingredient is the LINEAR cuts, whose absence is separately PROVED by GC-25's every-banked-symmetry-is-trivial-on-B_0)
hatch: The requirement is now exactly stated rather than closed: forcing the Higgs line needs THREE independent conditions LINEAR in h (or two plus the cubic). Since no symmetry provides them, they must come from a CONSISTENCY requirement linear in the closer's data -- an anomaly-type constraint on the coupling rather than a symmetry of it. Also named-not-run: when codex's T evaluator (R023) lands, check whether the object's own T is non-generic (identically vanishing determinant), given the banked SKEW ZERO and the rank-2 family law.

If the seam is ever re-posed on a sibling in the 112-family, compute that polygon first: it is a two-line check.

reader_quote: ABELIAN OR NOTHING, by Borel density
claim_killed: That the surviving gauge group -- the centralizer of rho(pi_1), I-26's untouched half -- is nonabelian, or has positive dimension beyond an abelian factor. The corpus invited this by recording B854's abelian u(1)^4 without drawing the distinction that makes it inapplicable.
kill_form: ABELIAN OR NOTHING, by Borel density. The object's geometric holonomy is discrete and faithful, hence a lattice in PSL2(C), hence ZARISKI-DENSE -- so its centralizer is contained in the centre of the ambient group. B854's u(1)^4 is the centralizer of 2T, the FINITE McKay image, which is a different object from the geometric holonomy; conflating them is what left the half looking open.
hatch: A representation that is NOT Zariski-dense -- i.e. not the geometric holonomy: a finite-image or reducible rho, where the centralizer genuinely can be large (B854's u(1)^4 is exactly such a case, correctly computed for its own object). Any revival must first say which representation it centralises, because the two answers differ and both are right about their own input.
